data.description: Patient on post-op day 2 following total knee arthroplasty developed severe uncontrolled pain (9/10) with hemodynamic instability (HR 117, BP 175/103), hypoxia (SpO2 91%), and fever (39.1C). Evidence of acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.8) and hyperkalemia (5.6 mEq/L) complicates analgesic options.
immediate_actions: Labs repeated for metabolic panel and troponin
Imaging performed to rule out pulmonary complications
data.outcome: Treatment escalation blocked; patient remains in distress

data.description: Attempted administration of excessive opioid doses (hydromorphone 64mg IV Q2H and sufentanil 30mcg sublingual Q1H) far exceeding maximum recommended limits. Standard hydromorphone dosing is 0.2–1mg IV Q2–3H; prescribed dose was 64x higher than upper limit. Sufentanil sublingual not standard in formulary and high-risk without specialist oversight. Decision support correctly blocked execution. Event triggered by erroneous pharmacy recommendation.
data.root_cause: Inaccurate clinical recommendation generation, possibly due to corrupted or hallucinated drug database entry.

Allergy status verified in EHR as life-threatening. Desensitization protocol considered per ID consult but not initiated. No adverse event occurred due to intervention halt.

Attempt to override documented penicillin anaphylaxis alert for administration of piperacillin-tazobactam in refractory cellulitis. Action denied by Admin phase. Patient has documented life-threatening penicillin allergy (2024-03-15, verified by allergist). Clindamycin failure noted; no approved alternative pathway initiated. Event highlights gap in allergy protocol and override governance.

Critical allergy alert override for penicillin-class antibiotic (piperacillin-tazobactam) in patient with documented anaphylaxis. Override performed per Infectious Disease consult recommendation due to clindamycin failure and refractory cellulitis. Desensitization protocol initiated.
data.action_taken: Allergy override with clinical justification and specialist consultation documented.
